title: Similar input profiles reduced flicker response prediction error in 32 selected fly visual cell types
abstract: We tested whether anatomical input-profile similarity predicts the flicker response shape of a held-out fly visual cell type. We linked public activity and two connectome distance tables by exact type names. Label checks excluded conflicting cells and table axes. The final sample had 271 neurons from 57 flies in 32 types. Nested validation chose neighbor counts and mixture weights without the held-out response. Combined input distances reduced mean shape error from 0.8333 for a global mean to 0.6974, a 16.3% reduction. Unrestricted and broad-class label tests each had Holm-adjusted p = 0.001. Combining specimens gave an uncertain added benefit. The female-only model had error 0.7048. The gain against a training-selected single source changed sign with a stricter cell count, and its fly resampling range included zero. A post hoc check with separate training and target flies retained a smaller 7.3% gain against the global mean. Input similarity provides a useful prediction baseline in this selected sample. Mean calcium responses, few cells per type, ambiguous labels, two anatomical specimens, and shared type definitions limit inference. The result does not establish a circuit mechanism or a rule across species, regions, or behavior. Code, source hashes, small source arrays, prediction tables, null scores, resampling draws, figures, and independent checks are included.

display.caption: Combined input-profile distances reduced held-out mean response-shape error in 32 selected types. Both refitted label tests had Holm-adjusted p = 0.001.
